output.title: When to offer 90-day mail order on a maintenance drug
output.draft_text:
Use this when a member calls about a maintenance medication and you are considering offering a 90-day mail order supply.

1. Verify the caller first. If the caller cannot be verified, do not discuss or set up mail order. Offer a callback only (see U-RX-EDU-002-05).

2. Confirm the drug qualifies.
- The drug must be a maintenance medication, meaning [definition or list source for maintenance medications, e.g., the plan's maintenance drug list].
- Specialty drugs do not qualify. They stay at Harbor Specialty Pharmacy and are not converted to mail order on this call (see U-RX-EDU-001-13).
- [Any other excluded drug categories, e.g., controlled substances, if applicable].

3. Confirm the member's eligibility.
- The member's plan must include mail order coverage: [how to confirm in the system].
- The member has been taking the medication for at least [minimum time on therapy or number of fills, if required].
- [Any other eligibility conditions, e.g., stable dose, no pending prior authorization].

4. Offer the option. Example wording: "Because this is a medication you take regularly, you may be able to get a 90-day supply through our mail order pharmacy, [mail order pharmacy name]."
- Describe cost only as directed: [cost or copay comparison guidance for 90-day mail order versus 30-day retail].
- Do not quote retail estimates from the pharmacy price page as mail order prices. Those estimates are for a 30-day supply at a preferred retail pharmacy (see U-WEB-FAQ-01).

5. If the member accepts, follow [process to set up mail order, e.g., new prescription from prescriber or transfer of existing prescription]. Tell the member to expect delivery in about [number of days].

6. If the member declines, document [documentation requirement] and continue the call.

[Any other excluded drug categories, e.g., controlled substances, if applicable]
[minimum time on therapy or number of fills, if required]

author_checklist: Confirm how advocates identify a maintenance medication, including the list or system source.
Confirm which drug categories, beyond specialty drugs, are excluded from 90-day mail order.
Confirm which plans include mail order coverage and how advocates check this.
Confirm whether a minimum time on therapy or number of prior fills is required before offering.
Confirm the name of the mail order pharmacy.
Confirm the approved cost or copay language for 90-day mail order versus retail.
Confirm the setup steps: new prescription versus transfer, and who contacts the prescriber.
Confirm documentation requirements for offers that are accepted and offers that are declined.
Confirm that the verification requirement and the specialty exclusion are consistent with U-RX-EDU-002-05 and U-RX-EDU-001-13.
Confirm whether advocates should offer mail order proactively or only when the member asks.
